clue.text: It could produce an itch to escape, say

indicators.note: 'say' asks us to speak the phrase and take a word that sounds the same

parts.note: to escape is to run away, a verb with the same sound as the insect

explanation.surface: Something that makes you itch for a getaway: wanderlust or restlessness.
explanation.definitionFit: A biting insect parasite whose bites leave skin irritated and scratchy.

clue.text: Stay relaxed if included in reporter's 'fodder pile'

indicators.note: 'included in' puts the reworked letters inside the next word

parts.note: first part of a hack, slang for a journalist

indicators.note: something relaxed has loosened its shape, so the word stay is rearranged

parts.note: end of a hack, slang for a journalist

explanation.surface: Someone is told to stay calm about what a journalist calls a pile of animal feed.
explanation.walkthrough: A hack is a journalist, so the reporter's word holds the rearranged stay. The quotation marks dress the definition up as a quote.
explanation.definitionFit: A stack of dried hay kept in a field as winter feed for livestock.

clue.text: Sentimental agent accepts cut

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so one word holds the other

parts.note: to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: A soppy secret agent takes a reduction in pay or a share of the deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloppy can describe gushing, mawkish feeling, as in a sloppy love song.

clue.text: Centre at York exhibiting suit

indicators.note: exhibiting means putting on show, so the letters are on display within the words

parts.note: runs across the three words, after the first letter

explanation.surface: A venue in York is putting on a display, perhaps of tailoring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' looks like clothing on show at the centre; here it is a plea, as in pressing one's suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A suit can be an earnest request or petition, which is what an entreaty is.

clue.text: Rod, circling one African country, stalls here

parts.note: first letter of bar, a rod

indicators.note: circling means going around, so the first word wraps the rest

parts.note: the international code for South Africa

explanation.surface: A rod is placed around an African nation, and something stops or stalls at that spot.
explanation.walkthrough: BAR wraps A plus ZA, the code for South Africa. 'stalls' reads as a verb but is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A market or charity sale is a place where many stalls are set up selling goods.

clue.text: Old writer takes care to show objectivity

parts.note: a pen is a writing tool
to mind is to take care, as in 'mind the step'

explanation.surface: An elderly author is careful in order to appear impartial.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with no fixed prejudices judges fairly, which is the quality of objectivity.

clue.text: Compliant power at fault

parts.note: P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: A compliant authority that is still to blame for what went wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A pliable person bends easily to others' wishes, readily going along with them.

clue.text: Down a foreign drunk

parts.note: happy can mean merry with drink

explanation.surface: Someone swallows a foreign drink, perhaps getting drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down a foreign drunk' reads as an imperative to swallow; 'Down' is the definition, meaning low in spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling down means being low, dejected or sad in mood.

clue.text: Stand back — one's covered in blue

indicators.note: 'back' tells us to read the word for blue the other way
something covered is wrapped by what covers it, so one goes inside

explanation.surface: Telling someone to step back because a person is covered in blue paint.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after one is 'is', joining it to 'covered in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised platform for speakers or a top table is a stand of a kind.

clue.text: Determine before spilling drop in ear

indicators.note: spilt contents scatter, so the letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Getting the eardrops ready before spilling any in the ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' looks like a word of time in the surface but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To preordain is to decree or settle an outcome in advance, ahead of time.

clue.text: Puerile shenanigans with — oh! — a Remainer?

indicators.note: shenanigans are mischief, so the letters are messed about

explanation.surface: Mocking childish antics by someone who voted to stay in the EU.
explanation.walkthrough: A Remainer voted in Britain's 2016 Brexit referendum to remain in the European Union; the question mark marks this as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A Remainer is a typical example of someone enthusiastic about Europe and EU membership.

clue.text: Turkish address housing a king with prominent nose

indicators.note: housing means giving a home to, so the title holds the other letters

parts.note: an Ottoman title of respect, used after a name

explanation.surface: A Turkish street address that houses a royal with a big nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaky describes someone having a large, hooked nose like a bird's bill.

clue.text: Flashy underwear's hot!

parts.note: H for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Showy lingerie is sexy.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after underwear is 'has', placing the next letter after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Brash means loud and showy, tastelessly ostentatious in appearance or manner.

clue.text: Only approved heads held in high regard, so anger on the way

indicators.note: held in means kept inside the jumbled word
high as in intoxicated, so the next word is jumbled
the heads of words are their first letters

parts.note: first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Only approved leaders are held in high esteem, so a public is angry about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held in high regard' reads as a single idiom; it must be split so 'high' works on regard.
explanation.definitionFit: Road rage is the fury drivers vent at other motorists while travelling.

clue.text: They're passed down clothes reportedly

indicators.note: 'reportedly' means as heard, so we want a word sounding like the clothes

explanation.surface: Hand-me-down clothing passed from older to younger siblings.
explanation.definitionFit: Units of heredity are inherited by children from their parents, generation to generation.

clue.text: See 23 Down
Fast as a crab?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: inclined to pinch with its claws

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second sense: a crab is given to nipping.
explanation.definitionFit: Nippy means quick and agile, and also playfully describes anything inclined to give a pinch.

clue.text: Run into trouble trapping energy particle

indicators.note: trapping means catching inside, so one letter goes within the rest
being in trouble suggests disorder, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Getting into difficulty by holding back power, as with a stuck machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A neutrino is a subatomic particle with almost no mass and no electric charge.

clue.text: See 6 Down
Swift game played against dwarf?

indicators.note: a game played is moved about, so its letters take a new order

parts.note: a dwarf is a kind of star, as in white dwarf; the question mark marks the example

explanation.surface: A fast match is played against a small opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swift' is not speed: it is Taylor Swift, the hugely famous American singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Taylor Swift is an example of an enormously famous entertainer, a celebrity of the highest order.

clue.text: Articles on a controversial illusionist that are used by setters

parts.note: THE, the definite article, made plural
Uri Geller, the spoon-bending performer whose claims of psychic power are disputed

explanation.surface: Newspaper pieces written about a disputed magician.
explanation.walkthrough: The S is loosely clued: 'Articles' is read as plural THEs. Crossword setters reach for thesauruses when hunting for synonyms.
explanation.definitionFit: Reference books of synonyms are standard tools for compilers of crossword puzzles.

clue.text: Rank, inferior stuff imported by South America

indicators.note: imported means brought in, so the stuff goes inside the other letters

explanation.surface: South America brings in rotten, inferior goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South America' looks like one place but is two pieces placed around the tat.
explanation.definitionFit: Status is one's standing or position in a hierarchy, much as rank is.

clue.text: Periodical reduced by Guardian wise guy

indicators.note: reduced means cut down, so only the short form of the periodical is kept

parts.note: the Guardian refers to itself as us

explanation.surface: A magazine's price or circulation is cut by the Guardian newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appears in the Guardian, so 'Guardian' is the paper speaking of itself: us.
explanation.definitionFit: A magus is a wise man, like the three Magi of the Nativity story.

clue.text: Element of one's deceitful character on the outside

indicators.note: on the outside means the Greek letter wraps around the rest

parts.note: first half of mu, the Greek letter
one is deceitful, read as I + LIE: 'I lie'
end of mu, the Greek letter

explanation.surface: Part of someone's deceitful personality shows on the surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' is a letter of the Greek alphabet, not a personality.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in one's element means being in one's natural surroundings or social environment.

clue.text: Jail outside America — my flight goes around it

indicators.note: outside means the jail word surrounds the abbreviation

parts.note: start of stir, slang for prison
end of stir, slang for prison

explanation.surface: A prison abroad, and a flight circling it, perhaps for a breakout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' sounds like a plane, but is a flight of stairs, which spirals round the shaft.
explanation.definitionFit: A staircase shaft is the vertical space that a flight of steps winds about.

clue.text: Northern folk of note perversely like being put first

indicators.note: being put first places that turned word ahead of the note
perversely means the wrong way round, so the word for like turns about

parts.note: the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Notable northerners who contrarily like to come first.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sami are the indigenous people of Lapland in the far north of Scandinavia.

clue.text: Cut end of grass and beard of barley

indicators.note: end of tells us to keep only the final letter

parts.note: an awn is the bristly tip on a cereal grain

explanation.surface: Mowing grass and trimming barley at harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beard of barley' looks like more crops to cut, but the bristles of barley ears are a single word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sawn is the past participle of saw, so something sawn has been cut.

clue.text: Beastly group put away stuff

parts.note: to wolf food is to put it away greedily
to stuff a bag is to pack it

explanation.surface: A rowdy gang told to tidy their things away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put away' reads as tidying up but means eating.
explanation.definitionFit: A band of hunting canines is literally a group of beasts, which roam together.

clue.text: Using mobile to ring politician is challenging

indicators.note: to ring is to encircle, so the rearranged letters surround the politician
mobile means able to move, so the word using moves into another order

explanation.surface: Phoning an MP on a mobile phone is a demanding task.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mobile' and 'ring' suggest phones; one stirs the letters and the other wraps them.
explanation.definitionFit: To impugn is to dispute or call into question someone's honesty or claims.

clue.text: Failure of foreign cable broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: An overseas cable TV transmission goes wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A debacle is a sudden, humiliating collapse or fiasco.
